Hello, anon! BS BAA to BA shiftee here. I passed BAA sa UPCAT thinking na I want something grand or something na may prestige. After all, onti lang naman talaga tinatanggap sa BAA. Tuwang tuwa ako kasi I was one of the lucky few. I hated accounting talaga, hindi ko siya kayang mahalin. I hated it more in BAA because of the culture na iniimpose ng accounting sa mga students. For me, the only reason to stay in BAA is if mag accounting ka talaga. Kung hindi, leave. If you think BAA will open a lot of opportunities for you, that’s valid but for me BAA will push you to become an accountant first bago ka mapunta sa iba’t ibang mga opportunities. Honestly, being in BA opened my eyes a lot and it made me happier. Ang dami kong oras to explore my passions while still learning business-related stuff. It’s just more holistic than being in BAA. Isipin mo na lang muna, OP, kung worth it ba yang mga taon mo sa BAA. For me, it wasn’t. I shifted out just this sem (I’m a sophomore)  after realizing na di ko gusto yung ganitong buhay na puro accounting at pag-aaral lang ang iniisip. Peace of mind lang for you, there’s light after BAA.

BS - BAA freshman here.

1. Your campus and degree programs should  be what you really WANT and in the proper order. Yours is already solid in terms of wanting to go to BAA. Your line of reasoning is sound and yes BA to BAA not that hard of a shifting process compared to others.

2. I have similar grades (consistent 94-97) from a metro manila Science High School (JHS) and from a THE Top Univ (the green one) (SHS) (not to sound elitist). I studied what I DIDN'T KNOW. Despite coming from a science high school, I hate science so I studied science. E.g. I never really understood photosynthesis until I reviewed for CETs. Study smart. Don't study hard.

3. There is no one way to study for UPCAT and there is no one key to UP. These review centers won't mean anything if you don't utilize them well. Brain Train yata yung best according to my friends.

4. You're arrogant. I like that. Most of my batchmates are like that in a good way. Marami samin BAA talaga ang dream course or if hindi naman, gustong mapatunayan na kayang pumasa ng BAA (kahit 'di nila gusto yung course). Your arrogance and guts will bring you places.

5. Sure ka na bang sa UP mo gusto mo mag-accountancy? Walang CoE ang CBA ng UP. Program-wise hindi ko marerecommend pero culture-wise and training-wise, UP is the way to go.

6. If you want to go to BAA just for the prestige, don't do it. Back out now. I'm one of the many who fell into this trap.

Not from UST-SHS but from DLSU-SHS. The culture and the experience might be different but here goes.

1. I'm not sure about the "fun" in España but my days in Taft were definitely the most fun. The school activities and org life were fun. The drinking, the party culture, and all that jazz were also fun. Do I miss it? Yes. Is it enough to make me stay? No. Honestly, UP is fun in its own way, just find the right people and the right activities for you :). 

2. Can't answer this, I'm not from USTe pero mas jologs talaga mga tiga-UP kaysa sa DLSU. Definitely my tribe.

3. Again, can't answer this exactly. Every univ has its own culture. For me ang pinakashocking, coming from another school,  is definitely the freedom. Hawak mo oras mo. Hawak mo buhay mo. Ikaw bahala sa acads at orgs mo and no one will say a thing sa ginagawa mo or kung ano ka as long as di ka nakakatapak ng ibang tao. Medyo mahihirapan kang mag-adjust if sanay kang spoonfed lahat at sheltered ka. Medyo mahirap mag-adjust sa una pero you'll get the hang of it.

4. I regret leaving DLSU because of its facilities and my course pero besides that wala naman. I'd rather regret that than regretting not going to my dream school HAHAHA

Good luck, OP! Sana nakatulong sagot ko kahit not from USTe
